In retrospect it was the only way to build a marketplace in our space at scale -- being broad in category increased the frequency of use of our product from once every couple years (how often do you need to hire a house painter?) to 8-12 times a year (the number of Thumbtack services an average American household hires annually). And being broad in geography allowed us to scale our marketplace as fast as possible, giving us the revenue, traffic, and thus experimental velocity we needed to bootstrap a great product. In our case we wouldn't have survived had we done it any other way.”
